clue.text: Breaking cups, restless female artists

indicators.note: something breaking falls to pieces, so the letters of the two words are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Restless women artists smash crockery in a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptress is a woman who sculpts, and sculptors are artists working in stone or clay.

clue.text: Device to get one sitting up?

definitions.text: Device to get one sitting up?

parts.words: Device to get one sitting up?
parts.note: read literally, a contraption that carries a seated person uphill, as on a ski slope

explanation.surface: It sounds like a gadget for helping someone rise from bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting up' suggests getting upright, but the passenger stays seated and is carried up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski-resort cable carries seated passengers uphill, which is exactly a device lifting people sitting on chairs.

clue.text: Go miles travelling around French city

indicators.note: letters travelling around move from place to place, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller covers many miles touring France and reaches a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: Means of transport for schools

definitions.meaning: to school someone is to teach or coach them, i.e. to train them

explanation.surface: School buses, perhaps: ways pupils get to school.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages pulled by engines are a mode of travel, and coaching or educating someone is the verb sense.

clue.text: Men not beginning to attempt record

indicators.note: the word Men loses its opening letter, the one it begins with

parts.note: an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Men without a head start nevertheless have a go at a world record.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is an item written into a register or log, so it is a record of something.

clue.text: A lot of water? Spot is heard

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken aloud, so a word for spot is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: Is there a big puddle? Look, one can be seen spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean or similar large body of salt water is a great quantity of water.

clue.text: Paying the bill for colony?

definitions.meaning: a community founded by settlers, a colony

explanation.definitionFit: Settling a debt is called settlement, and a newly founded community of settlers is likewise one.

clue.text: Friend getting millions — a reward for sporting achievement?

parts.note: a friend is a pal
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A pal earns a fortune as the prize for winning at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm frond was the ancient victor's prize, so the word still means a trophy or honour won.

clue.text: Charm with which a religious dissertation is read out

indicators.note: something read out is said aloud, so the phrase is replaced by the word it sounds like

parts.note: a tract is a short treatise, often religious; with a in front it gives A TRACT

explanation.surface: A preacher's essay is recited, charming its listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm people is to draw or allure them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Is representative of pietism so troubled about source of evil?

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the extra one
troubled letters are disturbed and stirred up, so pietism and so are rearranged
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Does piety, so disturbed by thoughts of evil, typify something?
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' signals the anagram and 'about' the wrapping; 'Is representative of' looks like part of the surface question but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise something is to be a typical example of it, standing for the whole.

clue.text: Quiet place associated with one of Henry's wives — it's ideal

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

parts.words: place associated with one of Henry's wives
parts.note: Catherine of Aragon was Henry VIII's first wife; Aragon is a region of Spain

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot linked to a Tudor queen is held up as perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII's first wife was Catherine of Aragon, a Spanish princess.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, something perfect that others are measured against.

clue.text: Sing melody badly apart from introduction

indicators.note: letters arranged badly are put in the wrong order, so the remainder is rearranged
the word melody is taken without its introduction, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sings a tune poorly, except for the opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from introduction' drops M, leaving ELODY, and 'badly' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is a particular Alpine style of singing, switching quickly between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Force acceptance of what motorist must do after work?

definitions.meaning: to drive a point home is to make someone accept it

definitions.text: what motorist must do after work?
definitions.meaning: literally, a commuter has to ... at the end of the day

explanation.surface: Insisting on a point, or just the commute back from the office.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hammering a point until it is grasped, and literally a commuter's evening journey by car.

clue.text: What this time without water ultimately brings?

definitions.text: What this time without water ultimately brings?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first letters go round the next one
ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of water is taken

explanation.surface: Going this long with no water would leave you parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: THIS plus T is wrapped round R, the last letter of water. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without drink for a time leads to a craving for liquid, the sensation of being parched.

clue.text: English maiden full of energy is showing obsession with self maybe

indicators.note: being full of something means containing it, so the first pair holds the second

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
go means energy, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A lively English girl displays self-absorption.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is preoccupation with one's own interests, a form of self-centredness.

clue.text: Stuff in good meat — good for starter

indicators.note: the second good supplies the opening letter, placed at the front

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Stuffing inside a good cut of meat, with something good to start the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is the noun for cloth, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a checked cotton fabric, and stuff is an old word for woven cloth.

clue.text: Food component gives excess energy to any number

parts.note: a glut is an excess or surplus
E is the physics symbol for energy
N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: An ingredient supplies surplus calories to any number of eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is a protein found in wheat and other grains, a constituent of many foods.

clue.text: Musician's original duet played with softened tone

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is its first one
played suggests being worked around freely, so the letters of duet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician's first duet was performed quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted music has its sound dampened, as when a mute is fitted to a trumpet.

clue.text: Greek character was first to turn up with word of gratitude

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to have been first, at the front, is to have led
ta is a British colloquial thank you

explanation.surface: A Greek who came first arrives to say thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Light shows a northern bird by lake

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A lamp reveals a seabird from the north standing by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, a source of light in an enclosed case.

clue.text: Brilliant colour displayed by vehicle left in group

indicators.note: in means put inside, so the vehicle and left go into the group

parts.note: a set is a group
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A brightly painted car stands out among a group of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid red hue, a bright shade on the colour spectrum.

clue.text: A year on river somewhere in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone spends twelve months on a river at a Scottish spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a coastal town in south-west Scotland, so it is a Scottish location.

clue.text: Raucous cry of a member of parliament?

definitions.text: Raucous cry of a member of parliament?

parts.words: Raucous cry of a member of parliament?
parts.note: a group of owls is called a parliament, so the member is an owl and its cry is meant

explanation.surface: It sounds like a heckling MP in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: The member is not an MP but an owl, since a flock of owls is called a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl's call, and also a jeering shout of derision, as from rowdy politicians.

clue.text: Means of identification of crop, we hear, more affected by cold?

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word for crop is swapped for its sound-alike

parts.note: a cereal is a grain crop such as wheat
numb from cold; more so is number

explanation.surface: Tagging a frostbitten harvest so it can be identified later.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is numb-er, comparative of numb, not the count.
explanation.definitionFit: A unique code stamped on a manufactured item lets it be identified and traced.
